newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Malaysia row reports see Singapore shares end weak.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia row reports see Singapore shares end weak.

text.p: Singapore shares closed down on Thursday, weakened by reports of a row with Malaysia.
"The row with Malaysia is what has done the damage today," said a dealer at a local broking house.
Singapore's barometer Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) dipped 12.68 points to 2,098.92 while the mainly Malaysian share tracking UOB OTC index fell 11.65 to 1,289.31.
Dealers said stocks were hit by reports on Wednesday that Malaysia had frozen all new bilateral ties with Singapore. The Malaysian government denied the reports on Thursday afternoon.
The denial helped the STII recover from an intraday low of 2,091.47, but with 295 losing issues swamping 74 gainers, dealers were unhappy with the entire episode.
"They should learn the famous phrase of American politicians -- 'no comment'," said one dejected dealer.
Malaysian shares were most active in moderate market volume of 185.6 million traded units. MBF Land and MBF Holdings respectively saw 9.1 million and 6.9 million units traded.
Creative Technology led losers, down Singapore $1.00 at S$13.40. Van der Horst warrants led gains, up S$0.76 at S$4.70.
